import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

data = {
    'Year': [2010, 2010, 2010, 2010, 2010, 2010,
             2011, 2011, 2011, 2011, 2011, 2011,
             2012, 2012, 2012, 2012, 2012, 2012,
             2013, 2013, 2013, 2013, 2013, 2013,
             2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014, 2014],
    'Vulnerable Employment (%)': [78.4, 65.2, 92.1, 83.7, 61.5, 55.3,
                         80.1, 67.8, 93.5, 85.2, 64.0, 57.9,
                         79.3, 69.5, 91.8, 86.4, 66.3, 59.6,
                         77.2, 71.1, 90.3, 84.9, 68.0, 61.2,
                         75.0, 72.6, 88.5, 82.7, 69.8, 63.4],
    'Sector': ['Agriculture', 'Construction', 'Domestic Work', 'Street Vending', 'Textiles', 'Food Processing'] * 5,
    'Informality Rate (%)': [62.3, 38.7, 75.5, 80.3, 35.8, 28.5,
                                  65.0, 42.0, 78.0, 55.0, 38.0, 31.2,
                                  63.8, 44.1, 76.2, 57.3, 40.2, 34.0,
                                  61.2, 46.3, 74.1, 54.8, 41.5, 36.2,
                                  59.5, 48.0, 72.0, 52.6, 43.7, 38.9]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Informality Rate (%)',
    y='Vulnerable Employment (%)',
    hue='Sector',
    size='Year',
    sizes=(50, 200),
    alpha=0.8,
    palette='husl'
)

scatter.set_title('Relationship Between Informality Rate and Vulnerable Employment (2010-2014)', fontsize=14, pad=20)
scatter.set_xlabel('Informality Rate (%)', fontsize=12)
scatter.set_ylabel('Vulnerable Employment (%)', fontsize=12)
plt.xticks(range(50, 100, 5))
plt.yticks(range(20, 85, 10))
plt.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0, fontsize=10)
plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig('output.png')

===  summary.txt
This scatter plot illustrates the relationship between the informality rate and vulnerable employment across various sectors from 2010 to 2014. The chart is titled "Relationship Between Informality Rate and Vulnerable Employment (2010-2014)" and presents data along two axes: the horizontal axis represents the informality rate in percentages, ranging from 50% to 95%, while the vertical axis shows the vulnerable employment rate in percentages, ranging from 20% to 80%.

Each data point on the scatter plot is color-coded to represent different sectors, including Agriculture, Construction, Domestic Work, Street Vending, Textiles, and Food Processing. A legend on the right side of the chart provides the color mapping for each sector. Additionally, the size of each data point corresponds to the year of observation, with larger points indicating more recent years (2014) and smaller points representing earlier years (2010).

The plot reveals several key patterns: Domestic Work consistently shows the highest informality rates, ranging from approximately 88.5% to 93.5%, with vulnerable employment percentages between 72% and 78%. Agriculture also exhibits high levels of both informality and vulnerable employment, with informality rates from about 75% to 78.4% and vulnerable employment rates from 59.5% to 65%. Street Vending displays high informality rates (82.7% to 86.4%) with vulnerable employment rates ranging from 50.2% to 57.3%. Construction, Textiles, and Food Processing sectors generally show lower informality and vulnerable employment rates compared to the other sectors. Construction's informality rates range from 65.2% to 72.6%, with vulnerable employment rates between 38.7% and 48%. Textiles and Food Processing have the lowest values, with Textiles' informality rates between 61.5% and 69.8% and vulnerable employment rates from 35.8% to 43.7%, while Food Processing ranges from 55.3% to 63.4% for informality and 28.5% to 38.9% for vulnerable employment.

The scatter plot effectively highlights a positive correlation between informality rates and vulnerable employment, indicating that sectors with higher informality rates tend to have higher rates of vulnerable employment.
